title: Ravana lifts the mountain
hook: Ravana tries to lift Shiva's mountain and ends up singing under it; why a temple's peak is for bowing
carry: the ego lifts; the devotee bows

segments.voice: Yesterday: abhaya mudra, the raised open palm that says don't be afraid. Your line was your worth isn't up for a vote: abhaya, no fear. Today, the top of year one.

Ravana is flying home in the Pushpaka, the flying chariot he has just taken from his own half-brother, and he has never been more sure of himself. Then, over a mountain in the far north, the chariot stops dead. It won't go on. Shiva's attendant Nandi steps out. This is Kailash, he says. Shiva and Parvati are here. Go around. Ravana laughs. Go around? He climbs down, gets his twenty arms under the mountain, and lifts.
screen: `THE CHARIOT STOPS OVER KAILASH.` → `GO AROUND.` → `RAVANA LIFTS THE MOUNTAIN.`

segments.voice: The mountain shakes. Parvati catches hold of Shiva. And Shiva, without even getting up, presses down with one toe. The mountain settles, and Ravana's arms are pinned beneath it. He roars with pain so loud the worlds tremble. His ministers tell him there's only one way out: praise the one you tried to move. So, pinned under the mountain, he sings to Shiva, and the old telling says he sang for a thousand years. At last Shiva lets him go and gives him a name: Ravana, the one who roared. At Ellora, in western India, a whole temple is cut down into one cliff of rock and named for Kailash itself, and on its side Ravana shakes the mountain while Shiva calmly holds it still with his foot. That's the shikhara idea: a temple's tower is often said to echo a holy mountain, Kailash or Meru. You don't climb it and stand on top. You come in under it, to the small dark room at its heart, and you bow. Hindus have a name for the part of you that tries to lift the mountain, and many teachers read Ravana here as just that: ahamkara, the I-maker, the ego that says mine, I did it. Ravana was strong enough to shake Kailash. Strength just wasn't the way in. Bowing was. Today is the top of year one: words, stories, practices, a whole scripture read through, the depths. The ahamkara would love to stand up here and say, done, I've got this. The tradition's move is the other one. At the top, you bow.
screen: `ONE TOE, AND THE MOUNTAIN SETTLES.` · `RAVANA, THE ONE WHO ROARED.` · `THE SHIKHARA ECHOES THE MOUNTAIN.` · `AHAMKARA: THE I-MAKER.` · `THE TOP OF YEAR ONE.` · then, large: `AT THE TOP, YOU BOW.`

segments.voice: Let the year come back in a few pictures: a word, a story, a flame. Notice the small voice that wants to say I did that. Then do what Hindus do on entering a temple or meeting an elder: bow, in your body if you can, or in your mind. If you pray, offer the whole year back to God. If you don't, simply let it be bigger than you, and rest there.
Shikhara, a mountain peak, and the name for the tower over a north Indian temple's shrine, often said to echo the holy mountain. You don't stand on it. You come in under it, and bow.
Your line: the ego lifts; the devotee bows. Ravana learned it under Kailash. Day three hundred thirty.

howItsDone: Many Hindus bow on entering a temple, before the shrine and before elders, and touch an elder's feet for a blessing; the Kailasa temple at Ellora, cut from a single rock, carries a famous carving of Ravana shaking Kailash.

chat.says: Nani made me touch Mama-ji's feet after i corrected his Gita quote in front of everyone 🙄 why bow to someone who got it WRONG??
options: a bow isn't a scoreboard. Ravana could lift Kailash and still had to bow to get free. it's for your ego.
you don't have to. bowing is only for elders who are right.
it's just manners. it has nothing to do with religion.
chat.meaning: Ravana had the strength to shake Kailash, but only praising Shiva set him free. Touching an elder's feet trains ahamkara, the ego; it isn't a score.

tie.story: Ravana tried to lift Shiva's mountain, got pinned under it, and was freed only when he sang Shiva's praise.
tie.friend: Priya can be right about the verse and still bow to Mama-ji: the bow is for her own ego, not his score.
tie.you: where would a bow cost you something this week?

Ravana.meaning: the ten-headed king of Lanka; his name means the one who roared

Kailash.meaning: Shiva's mountain home in the Himalaya

ahamkara.meaning: the I-maker: the ego that says mine, I did it

Ellora.meaning: rock-cut temples in Maharashtra, among them the Kailasa temple
